prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A skateboard with positive camber steering includes a frame and a board pivotally coupled to the frame. A steering assembly is coupled to the end portion of the frame and includes an upper truck arm, a lower truck arm, and at least one wheel. The upper truck arm and the lower truck arm are spaced apart relative to the frame, and the wheel has an axis of rotation. The upper truck arm and the lower truck arm are each rotatable about an axis of travel parallel to the skateboard's line of travel, and the upper truck arm is coupled to the wheel above the axis of rotation relative to the surface, with the lower truck arm coupled to the wheel below the axis of rotation relative to the surface. Thus the upper truck arm extends farther from the frame than the lower truck arm, thereby imparting a positive camber in the direction of steering.

The skateboard includes a frame and a board that is pivotally coupled to the frame, allowing the board to move relative to the frame during use. A steering assembly is attached to the frame and is configured to control the movement and steering response of the skateboard. The steering assembly includes an upper truck arm, a lower truck arm, and at least one wheel.

The upper truck arm and the lower truck arm are spaced apart from one another and are arranged to rotate about an axis of travel that is generally parallel to the direction in which the skateboard moves. The wheel is mounted between or in association with the upper and lower truck arms such that the arms support the wheel at different vertical positions relative to the wheel’s axis of rotation.

In particular, the upper truck arm is connected to the wheel at a location above the wheel’s axis of rotation, while the lower truck arm is connected to the wheel at a location below the wheel’s axis of rotation. This arrangement provides a stable steering structure and allows the wheel to respond to tilting or pivoting movement of the board and frame.

The upper truck arm extends a greater distance from the frame than the lower truck arm. As a result, the geometry of the steering assembly creates positive camber in the steering direction. This positive camber can improve turning behavior by positioning the wheel at an angled orientation during steering, thereby enhancing control, responsiveness, and stability while the skateboard is in motion.

A skateboard with positive camber steering includes a board configured to support a rider and a frame pivotally coupled to the board. The frame carries a steering assembly that allows the skateboard to turn in response to rider input, such as leaning or shifting weight on the board. The steering assembly includes a wheel mounted for rotation about a wheel axis, along with an upper truck arm and a lower truck arm that support and guide the wheel during steering movement.

The upper truck arm and the lower truck arm are connected to the wheel at different vertical positions relative to the wheel’s rotation axis. In particular, the upper truck arm is coupled to the wheel at a location above the axis of rotation, while the lower truck arm is coupled to the wheel at a location below the axis of rotation. Because of this arrangement, the upper truck arm extends a greater distance than the lower truck arm when measured from the steering structure to the wheel connection points.

This unequal arm geometry causes the wheel to assume a positive camber angle as the skateboard is steered. Positive camber means that the top of the wheel tilts outward relative to the bottom of the wheel during a turn. By producing positive camber during steering, the skateboard can provide improved turning response, enhanced stability, and a more controlled riding feel. The configuration may also help the wheel maintain more favorable contact with the riding surface during a turn, thereby improving handling and maneuverability compared with conventional skateboard steering arrangements.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a skateboard steering mechanism that uses upper and lower truck arms to create positive camber during turns.
counterfactuals.output: A skateboard steering mechanism is disclosed comprising a deck-mounted truck assembly having an upper truck arm and a lower truck arm operatively coupled between a base portion and an axle or wheel-supporting hanger. The upper and lower truck arms are arranged to define a linkage geometry that changes the angular orientation of the axle relative to the deck during steering. When the skateboard is leaned or otherwise steered into a turn, differential motion of the upper and lower truck arms causes the wheel-supporting hanger to tilt such that the outside wheel assumes a positive camber orientation relative to a riding surface. The induced positive camber reduces scrub, improves edge engagement, and enhances turning response, stability, and traction. In certain embodiments, the upper and lower truck arms pivot about spaced-apart axes and may be biased by resilient bushings, springs, or elastomeric members to provide self-centering and adjustable steering resistance. The mechanism may be incorporated into front and/or rear skateboard trucks and configured for carving, downhill riding, electric skateboards, or other wheeled board applications.

A **board or deck** is mounted to the frame so that the board can **pivot or tilt laterally** relative to the frame about a generally lengthwise pivot axis. When a rider shifts weight to one side, the board pivots relative to the frame and actuates the steering mechanism.

The **wheel rotation axis** therefore changes orientation during steering, producing a cambered wheel attitude rather than remaining upright.

In one implementation, the truck arms are arranged in opposed pairs, with each arm extending laterally outward from the frame to a respective wheel. The arms may be mounted so their pivot axes are inclined relative to vertical and/or arranged with suitable linkage geometry, causing the wheels to both steer and camber as the board is leaned. counterfactuals.prompt: In formal patent language, explain how a skateboard steering assembly can use truck arms rotating about axes parallel to the travel direction to produce positive camber.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a skateboard steering assembly comprises a deck-supporting base member and first and second wheel-supporting truck arms disposed on laterally opposite sides of a longitudinal centerline of the skateboard. Each truck arm is mounted to the base member for pivotal movement about a respective arm pivot axis extending substantially parallel to a normal forward travel direction of the skateboard. Thus, rather than rotating primarily about a vertical kingpin axis, each truck arm rolls or rocks about a generally fore-aft axis.

Each truck arm carries a wheel axle, or an axle-supporting portion, that is laterally offset from the corresponding arm pivot axis. By virtue of this offset, rotation of the truck arm about the fore-aft pivot axis changes the angular orientation of the wheel axle relative to the riding surface. More particularly, when the skateboard is leaned or when a steering input is applied to the deck, the base member causes the opposed truck arms to rotate about their respective longitudinal pivot axes. Such rotation raises one lateral portion of each axle-supporting arm and lowers another lateral portion thereof, thereby tilting the wheel plane with respect to vertical.

The pivot geometry is selected such that, during a steering or leaning condition, the upper portions of the wheels are displaced laterally outwardly relative to the lower ground-contacting portions of the wheels. Accordingly, the wheels assume a positive camber condition. In this condition, the wheel planes are inclined so that the tops of the wheels are farther from the skateboard centerline than the respective contact patches. The positive camber may be generated on one or both wheels of a truck, depending on the linkage configuration, arm phasing, and the direction of deck lean.

In a preferred arrangement, the truck arms are coupled to the deck or hanger by a cam, link, torsion member, or resilient biasing element arranged to coordinate rotation of the arms about the substantially longitudinal axes. As the rider shifts weight and rolls the deck, the base member rotates relative to the ground, and the linkage converts such deck roll into controlled rotation of the truck arms. Because the wheel axles are carried at positions spaced from the longitudinal pivot axes, the rotational motion of the arms produces a corresponding cambering motion of the wheels. The assembly thereby provides steering response and edge control while inducing positive camber during turning.

Stated differently, the steering assembly employs truck arms having roll axes generally aligned with the direction of travel. Rotation of the arms about those axes causes the wheel-supporting portions to sweep through an arcuate path in a transverse vertical plane. This arcuate displacement changes the inclination of the wheels relative to the support surface, and the geometry is arranged so that the resulting inclination is positive camber. Such positive camber can increase lateral compliance, modify tire or wheel contact characteristics, and provide a desired self-centering or carving feel during skateboard operation.
